notes:
- **The Savings tab prices your current setup with the live transcript you have chosen, and shows moving it to your graphics card as an offer.** The Current card used to keep the cost of a live stream you had already moved to this PC, and the map and the cards used different bases. Now the dots, your own dot and the cards share one price per meeting hour, the map says which live source it assumes (**Live transcript: this PC, free**), and a model on this PC that keeps up reads **A few seconds behind · this PC (free)**. **Live transcript by** shows what is set now and what an hour of it costs, and **Move the live transcript to your graphics card** has a **Switch**. See [Savings](/docs/usage-and-cost/#savings).
- **Each Savings tile says what you use and where the saving is.** **You use: AssemblyAI Universal-3.5 Pro**, then **Could save $X/mo with Deepgram Nova-3**, which jumps to that engine's card. The figure is the Current card's month minus that card's month, so a tile can no longer disagree with the cards under it.
- **New, off by default: Send only speech.** After a call, long quiet stretches of each side (five seconds or more, with a second kept at each edge) are left out before the recording goes to your speech service, so you pay for talking and not for long silences. A stretch is dropped only when the voice detector hears no speech there and its level stays near that side's own noise floor. Try it on a meeting first: **Compare on a meeting** has **This engine: whole recording vs. only the speech**, which shows the words that appear only in the whole run and what the cut saved. The recording on this PC is not changed. See [Send only speech](/docs/settings-reference/#transcript--summary).
